links.outcome: Sensitivity, NPV, specificity across operating thresholds 0.15, 0.125, 0.10 for triage
links.effect: Lowering threshold from 0.15 to 0.10 raised sensitivity 87.3% to 93.2% and NPV 87.0% to 91.3%, with specificity falling to 71.7%; trade-off deemed acceptable.
links.quote: By lowering the operating threshold, we increased sensitivity and NPV, at the cost of reduced specificity, a trade-off that was considered acceptable for a co-triage use case in primary care.

links.outcome: Threshold selection with clinician input balancing operational value and false negatives
links.effect: Threshold 0.1 chosen collaboratively with physicians and radiologists; sensitivity 93.19%, operational improvement 35.85% retained.
links.quote: Hence, the 0.1 threshold was deemed to have an acceptable sensitivity for safety and still retain acceptable potential operational improvement to yield value in implementation.

links.outcome: Local threshold tuning versus vendor default on representative polyclinic data
links.effect: Default 0.15 gave sensitivity 87.3%, NPV 87.0%; tuned 0.10 gave sensitivity 93.2%, NPV 91.3%, specificity 71.7%.
links.quote: We found that the threshold required for optimal performance of Lunit CXR as a co-triage tool was different from the default threshold of 0.15 set by Lunit.

links.outcome: Performance on representative local data against radiologist reference standard
links.effect: At 0.15, AI sensitivity 87.3% vs radiologist report 80.7%; specificity 85.0% vs 85.9%.
links.quote: At the default recommended threshold, Lunit INSIGHT CXR3 achieved greater sensitivity than the radiologist (87.3% vs 80.7%) with comparable specificity (85.0% vs 85.9%).

links.outcome: AI sensitivity and NPV compared with working radiologist reports on same data
links.effect: At 0.125, sensitivity 90.10% vs 80.7% and NPV 89.01% vs 81.66% for radiologist, with non-overlapping CIs.
links.quote: At threshold 0.125, Lunit-enabled workflow demonstrates superior performance compared with the radiologist report, with significantly higher sensitivity (90.10% (95% CI 87.19% to 92.86%) vs 80.7% (95% CI 76.83% to 84.42%)) and NPV (89.01% (95% CI 85.71% to 92.05%) vs 81.66% (95% CI 77.95% to 85.24%)), with non-overlapping CIs in both metrics confirming the statistical significance of these differences.

links.outcome: Reporting performance metrics with CIs at multiple operating points to decision-makers
links.effect: CIs across thresholds informed stakeholder threshold decision; non-overlapping CIs gave stronger justification than point values.
links.quote: CIs, as shown in figure 3 , were useful for the decision-making process, with non-overlapping CIs providing stronger justification, as compared with point values.

links.outcome: Planned silent deployment on live CXRs after retrospective threshold selection
links.effect: Team prepared for silent deployment to further evaluate performance; results not yet reported.
links.quote: After the decision was finalised, the team prepared for a ‘silent deployment’ of the AI model on live CXRs to further evaluate the performance.
